### Observed differences

- The elapsed time between the completion of A02 and the completion of A07, when they occur as consecutive events, roughly halved. In the earlier window these gaps averaged about 0.86 hours (median about 0.88; middle half between about 0.78 and 0.93 hours); in the later window they averaged about 0.43 hours (median about 0.44; middle half between about 0.37 and 0.48 hours) — a drop of about 0.43 hours, roughly 50 in 100 of the earlier level, with the middle halves of the two distributions no longer overlapping. [TWAIT001]
- How often this consecutive pair is observed barely moved: about 32 of 200 traces in the earlier window (about 16 in 100) versus about 35 of 200 in the later window (about 18 in 100). The change lies in the duration of the gap, not in how often the pair occurs. [TWAIT001]
- Control-flow screening of 55 units produced no qualifying items (about 0.27 would be expected by chance alone), so no structural, ordering or participation difference was detected alongside the timing shift. [TWAIT001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a timing change on the step between A02 and A07: in the later window, the elapsed time from the completion of A02 to the completion of A07 (when consecutive) is about half of what it was, falling from about 0.86 to about 0.43 hours on average. [TWAIT001]

Supporting signs: the indicator measures exactly this elapsed time, so the evidence is direct; the shift is consistent across the whole distribution (every quartile lower, non-overlapping middle halves); it rests on 32 versus 35 observations; and it is larger than in about 9995 of 10000 random re-splits of the pooled data. The screening context fits: the time family produced one item where about 0.009 were expected without change (roughly 1 in 100 screenings of this size would yield such an item by chance), while control flow produced none where about 0.27 were expected. The timing difference therefore stands well above what chance re-splits typically produce, and it is not accompanied by a detected structural change — consistent with a timing change, which needs no structural counterpart. [TWAIT001]

Limitations: the profile is based on only about 32–35 gap observations per window (roughly 16–18 in 100 traces), and elapsed time between consecutive completions conflates waiting and processing, so the evidence cannot show whether the reduction came from waiting, from handling, or from this pair now occurring in faster kinds of cases. That case-mix explanation is weakened by the absence of detected control-flow differences but cannot be fully ruled out. [TWAIT001]

Other differences: the number of observed A02–A07 gaps rose slightly, from 32 to 35 per 200 traces (about 16 to 18 in 100), a small shift consistent with sampling variation. [TWAIT001]
